> 大國者下流，天下之牝，天下之交也.

Chapter 60 was the fish in the pan. Chapter 61 is water: where it goes.

## 下流 is the lower reach

流: 水行也 — water moving.

下流 is not "low conduct." It is the downstream segment of a river — the place every upstream is already heading toward.

The image is exact: a river does not decide to be downstream. It is downstream because of the terrain, and by being so it receives everything.

## 天下之牝

牝 is the female animal — and in this chapter, specifically the one standing beside.

The claim: 牝常以靜勝牡，以靜為下. The female by stillness overcomes the male, and by stillness takes the lower place.

This is not flattery about gentleness. It is a statement about position: what waits in place does not have to move to be found.

## 交

天下之交也 — again the crossed legs. The place where all roads meet and each party can turn away.

## 或下以取，或下而取

> 故大國以下小國，則取小國；小國以下大國，則取大國。故或下以取，或下而取.

Four characters differ by one: 以 and 而.

下以取 — descending in order to take.
下而取 — descending, and thereby taken.

The same motion, two directions of outcome. The one who descends to secure something gets it only as long as he keeps descending; the one who descends and is received has been taken in without effort.

## 大國不過欲兼畜人，小國不過欲入事人

The large state wants only to 兼畜 — gather and feed. The small state wants only to 入事 — enter and serve.

Both wants are modest, and both are satisfied by the same movement. Which is why the conclusion is not a compromise but an identity: 夫兩者各得其所欲.

## 大者宜為下

> 夫兩者各得其所欲，大者宜為下.

宜: 所安也 — the place where a thing comes to rest.

So the last line is not "the great should be humble." It is: for the great, being lower is where it settles.

That changes the register entirely. Humility is a moral posture that has to be maintained, and maintaining it is work. 宜 is a location: the great power that descends is not performing an attitude; it has found the position where it is stable.

A large thing is unstable at the top — it has farther to fall and more to defend. At the lower reach it is exactly where the weight already goes.

## Why the chapter follows 60

60: the pan that should not be turned.
61: the reason a large thing can afford not to turn: it is downstream by nature, and everything is already coming to it.

The large state's temptation is to reach upstream. The chapter's answer is that its position is downstream, and that position is what it has instead of force.

## The one asymmetry

The chapter is careful: both sides benefit, but only one of them is told where to settle.

The small state's descent is a necessity; the large state's descent is a choice that has a resting place. That asymmetry is why the last line is addressed to the 大者 — the one for whom descending is not obvious.

## A test

Take the position where you hold the most power — in a team, a family, a negotiation. Ask whether you are standing at the top defending it, or downstream receiving. The difference shows up in how much you have to keep doing.
